## Validation and assumptions

No relevant articles were supplied. I found a 2015 Cochrane review and screened a targeted subset of its references. Relative recall was **16/16 (100%)** on the development set and **5/5 (100%)** on the held-out validation set. The validation set is semi-independent because both sets came from that review’s reference pool; it is not an independent benchmark.

I assumed “anxiety-related disorders” includes core anxiety disorders plus OCD and PTSD. No minimum duration was specified, so follow-up duration remains a screening decision. The tested long-term/follow-up block cut the count by 55%, but its loss sample included an eligible CBT study with outcomes at 3, 6, and 9 months. I left that block out. The final count exceeds the standard 10,000-record workload budget.

The internal critique was same-context, not a fresh-context review. This draft still needs PRESS peer review by an information specialist before use. The counts use the current PubMed index with an Entrez-date bound; they do not reconstruct the index exactly as it existed in 2017.
